system_label: Arm B1: one agent with generic evidence tools only (no checks)

findings.rationale: The immunization registry export was written to a non-standard staging directory /var/tmp/xfer and then uploaded. Earlier monthly files with the same naming pattern (imm-registry-100/101/102, Aug to Oct, fs_stat) suggest a recurring process, which points to a routine job rather than a one-off. The evidence does not establish intent or that the data went anywhere other than the approved gateway.
alternative_explanations: Recurring registry submission workflow using a staging directory
Staging chosen by the export tool's default path
verifier_notes: references resolve; no allegation is made

findings.rationale: Account kcole logged in on the shared station tty1 during the 13:11 to 13:13 export and upload. Badge records show kcole's badge (B-1633) out at 11:17 and back in at 11:53 with no later badge-out until 15:03, so the badge was present. Remote VPN sessions are not covered by badge records, and console credentials at this station have been found written down before. Who was at the keyboard is not established.
alternative_explanations: another person used the kcole credential
verifier_notes: references resolve; no allegation is made

findings.rationale: Workstation auth.log was rotated by scheduled logrotate at 09:08:01 (keep 1, rotated copy .1 retained). The collector holds a continuous sequence (seq 1 to 53) of the workstation auth.log lines with no gap, so no evidence of local log removal was found for this file.
verifier_notes: references resolve; no allegation is made

findings.rationale: A 22.5 MB outbound flow from 10.20.0.10 to 10.20.0.45:873 (stor-nas-01, approved for backup and log archive). Destination is approved, so this is consistent with policy. The source host is not named in the evidence, so host is given as the workstation only as a placeholder and is not confirmed.
verifier_notes: a deterministic check supports this observation; it is not an incident allegation

findings.rationale: Account kcole ran a bulk export of the immunization_registry dataset (11.79 MB per records app) to /var/tmp/xfer and uploaded it with curl to 10.20.8.20:80 (lab-gw-01), 11.79 MB on the tap flow. 10.20.8.20 is an approved destination for laboratory and registry submissions, so the destination is not a policy violation on the brief's rule. The transfer is still a bulk export of clinic registry data and the business purpose is not confirmed by the evidence.
alternative_explanations: Routine registry submission to the approved lab/registry gateway
verifier_notes: a deterministic check supports this observation; it is not an incident allegation
